sources.name: Zenodo, PyTorch Image Models (timm) software archive

profile_text.body:
PyTorch Image Models, known as timm, is an open-source project hosted on GitHub under huggingface/pytorch-image-models. It describes itself as the largest collection of PyTorch image encoders and backbones, and it includes scripts for training, evaluation, inference, and export, along with pretrained weights. Model families named on the site include ResNet, ResNeXT, EfficientNet, NFNet, Vision Transformer (ViT), MobileNetV4, MobileNet-V3 and V2, RegNet, DPN, CSPNet, Swin Transformer, MaxViT, CoAtNet, and ConvNeXt. The project states that all model architecture families include variants with pretrained weights, and that some variants ship without weights by design rather than as a bug.

Recent work described on the site includes adding Sapiens2 ViTs with EVA and NaFlexViT support, both with native timm Hub weights, credited to Yonghye Kwon, and adding model definitions and pretrained weights for EUPE ViT (DINOv3-style) and ConvNeXt models, referencing the Efficient Universal Perception Encoder paper. Other entries cover a CSATV2 model credited to a GitHub user, described as lightweight but high resolution with a DCT stem and spatial attention, EfficientNet-X and EfficientNet-H B5 weights from a hyperparameter search comparing AdamW and Muon, and fixes for stale evaluation attention bias caches, pruned model feature metadata, dilated max-pool padding, and asymmetric loss gradient mode. The site also mentions a dynamic global pool implementation that selects among average pooling, max pooling, average plus max, or concatenation of average and max at model creation, with adaptive average pooling as the default and compatibility with pretrained weights.

The project is recorded as a non-profit open-source foundation founded in 2019, with source references to its GitHub repository and a Zenodo software archive. No products, lawsuits, or MCP servers are recorded for it.
